issue.title: tests/shard_timings.json is 19.98% off the 20% file-count drift limit: the next new test file fails test_test_shards
issue.description:
`tests/shard_timings.json` records `measured_file_count` = 3513, but the tree now discovers 4215 test files at master 4255afbb05: 19.98% drift against a hard 20% limit in `tests/test_test_shards.py::test_committed_table_measured_count_has_not_drifted_too_far`. The table is one new test file away from failing that test for everyone; adding a single file (4216 files, 20.01%) makes it fail deterministically with "discovered file count 4216 has drifted 20% from the table's measured 3513 (run `just refresh-shard-timings`)".

`just refresh-shard-timings --check` also reports the table as "stale relative to this host's local recordings". The CI ratchet workflow (`shard-timings-ratchet.yml`, per tools/refresh_shard_timings) is supposed to keep it fresh; either it has not run since the file count grew, or its trigger only fires on assignment change / 14-day age.

Fix: refresh the committed table from a quiet host (or let the ratchet publish), and consider having the ratchet also trigger on file-count drift well before the 20% limit (for example at 10%) so an unrelated change never becomes the one that trips the test.

Observed while adding `tests/ace/tui/test_update_completion_toast.py` (the 4216th file) for the Update-panel provider detail work.

task_type_fields.impact: Any agent or PR that adds a test file gets a red scoped lane / master gate on an unrelated node, and the stated remedy (just refresh-shard-timings) rewrites an 800-entry data file measured on whatever host runs it.
task_type_fields.repro: Count test files: the committed table measures 3513, the tree discovers 4215 (19.98%). Add any new tests/**/test_*.py file and run: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_test_shards.py::test_committed_table_measured_count_has_not_drifted_too_far. It fails with drift 20% (20.01%).

evidence.note: Independent reproduction while landing epic sase-14l (proposed by phase bead sase-14l.3, note #2). The predicted crossing has happened: at master 383f2c282 the gate is now RED, not merely close. tests/test_test_shards.py::test_committed_table_measured_count_has_not_drifted_too_far fails with 'discovered file count 4219 has drifted 20% from the table's measured 3513' (assert 0.20096783376031882 <= 0.2). Deterministic arithmetic over a committed table, not a flake; fix is just refresh-shard-timings.

Independently reproduced on clean origin/master e1ba4851c (git worktree, no local changes): tests/test_test_shards.py::test_committed_table_measured_count_has_not_drifted_too_far fails deterministically, so the drift limit is now actually exceeded rather than 19.98%; every new test file added on top of it is a second reason it stays red.

Independent report from sase-11y.10.1.4 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note #2: 4222 discovered vs 3513 measured). Reproduced by the sase-11y.10.1 land agent on master 3a08b8681 on 2026-09-21: tests/test_test_shards.py::test_committed_table_measured_count_has_not_drifted_too_far fails deterministically, and every just check scoped lane that selects it goes red.

sase-14n.15 land (proposed by sase-14n.15.2): test_committed_table_measured_count_has_not_drifted_too_far now fails outright at master 1567269ca (sase-14n.15.2 measured 4249 files vs committed 3513, 21% past the 20% gate); reproduced in sase tool run check 49a0b5a3f03c73ae254e349f4616a50e.

Threshold now breached on master 7c763a2e7: discovered 4331 files vs measured 3513 = 23% drift, so test_committed_table_measured_count_has_not_drifted_too_far fails for everyone. Reproduced during fix_ten_master_check_failures verification (fails identically on the clean tree and with the fix applied); unrelated to that change.

sase-165 land agent (relaying sase-165.4/.5 PROPOSED FOLLOW-UPs): reproduced at master 8d1779a3e on 2026-09-22 — tests/test_test_shards.py::test_committed_table_measured_count_has_not_drifted_too_far now fails deterministically in isolation (drift limit crossed), reddening every just check.

Ran just refresh-shard-timings while landing the Agents status row polish plan (202609/agents_status_row_polish.md), whose two required new test files pushed drift to 23%: table now records 4158 measured files and tests/test_test_shards.py passes 33/33. If this bead's worker re-runs the refresh at land time, expect the count to move again.
